source.title: Tropical Cyclone Attributes in Sparse Autoencoder Features of an AI Weather Model
source.authors: Jia-Pei Liu; Rui-Dong Li; Ting Sun; Guang-Heng Ni

page_placements.theme: Concepts carried by groups of SAE latents, with single latents serving several related categories (not neurons)

record.tranche_reason: The study examines sparse-autoencoder feature organization in a weather model, but does not test the claim versions about language-model neuron poles, explanation fidelity, attribution graphs, or the cited vision-model example.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about how cyclone attributes relate to GraphCast SAE features. These are relevant to internal feature organization generally, but do not measure the neuron-pole job shares or behaviors named by any claim version. The paper also cites findings from other work; those are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study trains sparse autoencoders on GraphCast weather-model hidden states and correlates SAE features with tropical-cyclone attributes. It does not audit neuron poles, does not study language models or InceptionV1, builds no attribution graphs, and does not score natural-language explanations. No claim version is tested. 'Discusses' is generous: the paper never engages the essay or the neuron-explanation literature, so 'cites_only' or plain T6 non-use is the closer fit. The relation is kept as recorded, with this caveat.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find a distributed but partially bundled organization of cyclone-attribute relations across SAE features. It recurs across independent SAEs and all 16 processor layers. In deeper layers, the F1-leading features align better with position and pressure structure six hours ahead.
record.recipe_differences: The study probes GraphCast weather-model hidden states with sparse autoencoders and measures correlations between SAE activations and cyclone attributes. It does not audit language-model neuron poles or test natural-language neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported organization varies across independent SAE fits in feature identity, ranking, and concentration; the authors state that they did not test sensitivity to SAE settings or the selected-subset size.

fits_no_version.finding: In the Layer-8 GraphCast SAE, position and pressure-structure relations spread over modest feature sets (Neff 18.5 and 59.5), their overlap is concentrated (Nshared 4.38), and intensity is very broad (703.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Physical-event attributes in an AI weather model are distributed across multiple SAE features with partial bundling, not one feature per attribute.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five independent Layer-8 SAE fits, Top-4 effective feature numbers recur in similar ranges despite changes in feature identity and ranking.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Organization of attribute relations across SAE features is reproducible across seeds even when individual features are not.

record.problems: The analysis covers one model, two years (2018–2019), and 205 cyclones. It measures correspondence rather than causal use of features; no intervention or ablation is performed. The authors did not test sensitivity to SAE settings or to the selected-subset size.
record.rows_left_out: No results directly testing the listed claim versions were reported. Other non-version results, including the all-layer profiles, individual-feature summaries, and forecast-time comparisons, were omitted because they concern GraphCast cyclone-attribute correspondence rather than the claim's neuron-pole or explanation outcomes.
